responses.response: Keep the baseline config shape intact and make the smallest possible project-specific edits. In this workspace the reusable sources live under `projects/shared/`, so from `projects/payments/likec4.config.json` reference shared specs and images with project-relative paths such as `../shared`, not absolute paths and not workspace-rooted paths. Preserve the existing include block and any existing image alias entries exactly as they are, then add only the new entries you need under distinct names so current imports keep resolving. The safe rule is: extend the baseline config, do not replace it.

Use a two-step split. First, move the monolith into the repo’s minimal baseline used by `projects/template/`: put elements and relationships in `system-model.c4`, and put views in `system-views.c4`. Second, when the model is stable, split it the way `projects/spec-showcase/` is organized: `actors-systems.c4` for actors and top-level systems, `containers.c4` for containers, `components.c4` for components, `context-views.c4` for C1 views, `container-views.c4` for C2 views, and `component-views.c4` for C3 views. If Use Cases, deployment, or operations are still small, leave them in `system-views.c4` at first; once they grow, give them dedicated files such as `use-cases.c4`, `deployment.c4`, and `operations.c4`.

Follow append-only edit rules. Keep the existing `include.paths` entries in the current order (`../shared`, then `../platform-shared`) and add the new shared source after them unless you explicitly want the new source to take precedence. Do not rename, delete, or repoint any current icon/image aliases; add the new source’s aliases under a unique prefix so no existing alias changes meaning. Keep every path relative to `projects/payments/likec4.config.json`, not to the workspace root. In short: preserve order, preserve old aliases, add new namespaced aliases only.

No, not by itself. It is enough for wiring shared includes into one project config, but adding a second LikeC4 project is also a workspace-layout problem. Pair it with the workspace’s multi-project organization capability, and if you need to confirm the existing baseline first, use the workspace’s project-structure capability before doing the config edits. Use this skill for the include and shared-source wiring, not for the whole multi-project design.

To preserve current resolution, keep `../shared` before `../platform-shared` in `include.paths`; that keeps the existing shared source in the same precedence position. Then fix the collision in `imageAliases`, not by reordering includes: keep every current shared alias name mapped to the current shared image, and add new platform aliases under different names such as a `platform-` prefix. That way old references still resolve exactly as before, while new references can opt into the platform-shared images explicitly. Do not overwrite or rename the old shared alias keys unless you are prepared to update every existing reference.

The smallest safe edit is: append `"../platform-shared"` immediately after `"../shared"` in `include.paths`, then add only new platform-prefixed entries to the existing `imageAliases` object. Example fragment to merge into the current file: `{ "include": { "paths": ["../shared", "../platform-shared"] }, "imageAliases": { "platform-logo": "../platform-shared/images/custom/logo.svg" } }`. Keep every existing shared alias entry unchanged; if `logo` already exists for `../shared`, do not replace it—add `platform-logo` (or another namespaced key) instead.
